payoff: Turn the SYS-008 OpenAPI design into ten actual HTTP checks and fail on status, header or schema regressions.
learningOutcomes: untuk /transfers & /accounts uji 200/201/400/401/403/404/409/422/500 berdasarkan spec; pastikan error code dan response schema stabil.
mentalModel: OpenAPI expected contract -> actual HTTP response -> status/header/body assertions -> intentional mutation guards; testing a stub cannot prove Spring implementation.
relationshipGraph: SYS-008 OpenAPI paths -> TST-019 operation matrix -> ephemeral Node HTTP server -> fetch requests -> status/Location/WWW-Authenticate/Problem Details -> schema assertions -> mutation detection.

concepts.title: Operation response matrix
concepts.mechanism: The external OpenAPI response map enumerates allowed statuses for each method/path. Although RFC 9110 defines 422, SYS-008 has no 422 response declared.

concepts.title: Real loopback HTTP verification
concepts.mechanism: An ephemeral Node server receives ten actual HTTP requests and returns status, headers and JSON over a network socket; this fixture does not represent Spring MVC.

concepts.title: Error and response drift detection
concepts.mechanism: Responses are checked against an explicit schema subset with required fields, primitive types, enums and patterns; deliberate incorrect statuses, missing 401 challenge and bad amount types must fail.

misconceptions: 422 is defined by HTTP but absent from the SYS-008 OpenAPI response map.
A passing static OpenAPI checker does not observe actual HTTP.
An educational server with hard-coded tokens does not implement OAuth, authorization or payment processing.
A passing happy path does not ensure error response safety and compatibility.
practice: Build operation-specific status and header expectations from SYS-008.
Run actual HTTP POST/GET success and negative paths on loopback.
Reject three intentionally broken responses and document the 422 gap.

coverage.taughtAt: Three V3 objectives: response oracle, wire matrix and mutation-based schema/error checks
coverage.assessedAt: Ten HTTP exchanges, three negative mutations, five self-check questions and contract-gap declaration
coverage.evidenceExpected: 200/201/400/401/403/404/409/500 observed on local stub; 422 not declared; response Content-Type, required fields, headers and Problem status correct.

coverage.taughtAt: Independent GET account checks and response error/schema drift
coverage.assessedAt: New account 200/404 scenario plus independent production Spring contract test challenge
coverage.evidenceExpected: A different account case, demonstrated negative mutation detection, and explicit runtime evidence boundary.

segments.objective: Compare the required workbook status set to the exact responses promised by SYS-008 OpenAPI.
segments.whyItMatters: An API test based on a guessed code is not a check of the public contract.
segments.mentalModel: The response matrix belongs to each method/path in OpenAPI, not to an arbitrary global list of HTTP status codes.
segments.explanation: SYS-008 promises POST transfer 201/400/401/403/409/500, GET transfer and account 200/401/403/404/500. RFC 9110 defines 422 Unprocessable Content but this API does not declare it. A TST-019 test must explicitly report the mismatch, not fabricate a 422 success or silently change 400. 201 also requires Location while 401 requires WWW-Authenticate.

workedExample.problem: The workbook requests a 422 test case, but the POST /transfers response map has no 422.

steps.action: Read the three SYS-008 operations and enumerate response keys.
steps.reason: Only the checked-in design specifies observable promises.
steps.expectedResult: Exactly three operation matrices, including GET 404.

steps.action: Check POST 422 against the declared response keys.
steps.reason: An RFC-defined status is not automatically supported by this particular API.
steps.expectedResult: Report 422 as undeclared rather than a passing test.

steps.action: Add Location and WWW-Authenticate to the matrix.
steps.reason: A correct HTTP status can still have an invalid header contract.

guidedPractice.prompt: Can the current SYS-008 contract legitimately be tested as promising HTTP 422?
hints: 422 is defined by RFC 9110 but not declared by this operation.
guidedPractice.explanation: No. Keep malformed POST input on documented 400 until a versioned contract change deliberately introduces 422.

independentChallenge.prompt: For GET /accounts/{id}, evaluate whether an undocumented 409 response is contract-compliant.
expectedEvidence: A per-operation status/header matrix with an explicit explanation of the 422 gap.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: GET account 409 is a different operation and failure category than POST transfer 422.

segments.firstAction: List the exact response keys of POST /transfers from SYS-008.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Assuming HTTP 422 is supported simply because it exists in the standard.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: The standard lists possible statuses, not commitments made by an individual OpenAPI document.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Validate each operation's declared response map and request a specification change for a new status.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Three explicit operation matrices match OpenAPI and 422 is labeled absent.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Read the actual paths object instead of relying on an external checklist.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Run live local HTTP requests against the response matrix.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Begin from POST 201 and its two error families, then inspect GET.

segments.objective: Run ten real HTTP requests to a local server and verify positive and negative responses.
segments.whyItMatters: Static specification checks cannot prove what an HTTP server sends on the wire.
segments.mentalModel: Arrange isolated server -> Act network fetch -> Assert status, headers and schema -> Release socket.
segments.explanation: The fixture binds to 127.0.0.1 on a random port, handles POST/GET transfers/accounts with in-memory resources, and uses fixed bearer strings only for demonstration. It performs 10 live HTTP requests covering statuses 200/201/400/401/403/404/409/500. The 201 response provides a resource URI and PENDING body, not completed financial settlement.

workedExample.problem: A new transfer is created, read again, and its account is retrieved through real HTTP.

steps.action: Run node labs/TST-019/http-contract.mjs from the repository root.
steps.reason: This starts an actual ephemeral HTTP server.
steps.expectedResult: The program records ten successful round-trip checks.

steps.action: Check POST Location points at the new transfer resource.
steps.reason: 201 Created must identify the created representation.

steps.action: Request missing credentials, forbidden and absent resource cases.
steps.reason: Negative paths must produce stable machine-readable outcomes.
steps.expectedResult: 401 challenge, 403 denial and 404 missing resource with Problem Details.

guidedPractice.prompt: Why does reading an OpenAPI example not prove a running service returns Location?
hints: The example is a JSON declaration, not a network exchange.
Inspect actual headers returned by fetch from the HTTP server.
guidedPractice.explanation: A client must send a request to the running endpoint and examine the observed status and Location header; the educational server is still not Spring MVC.

independentChallenge.prompt: Add a new GET account fixture and verify both 200 and 404 with different IDs.
expectedEvidence: 10 HTTP checks with statuses and headers plus an independent account request variant.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: Read a new account not used in the transfer creation example.

segments.firstAction: Execute the Node loopback fixture and inspect the response summary.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Claiming a test of the local in-memory stub proves Spring controller routing or JWT verification.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: The actual Spring runtime, DB connection and token verifier are never loaded by this exercise.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Run the same contract assertions against an independently implemented target service before claiming integration coverage.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: All ten requests complete on a loopback socket and the server is closed cleanly.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Check whether the ephemeral HTTP bind, JSON parser or assertion failed.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Prove the checker rejects deliberately malformed responses.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Follow the path from spec to request to actual header and JSON body.

segments.objective: Reject invalid Problem Details, missing 401 challenge and a breaking amount type mutation.
segments.whyItMatters: A test that passes a broken response cannot protect client contracts.
segments.mentalModel: The oracle validates independently of the handler: real HTTP status, media type, schema shape and error member status must agree.
segments.explanation: A selected OpenAPI schema subset validates required fields, string/integer types, patterns, enums and additionalProperties. Three deliberate mutations are rejected: HTTP 409 with body status 500, 401 without WWW-Authenticate, and JSON amount as a number instead of decimal string. The checker is not full JSON Schema evaluation or real consumer compatibility testing.

workedExample.problem: The HTTP response is 409 Conflict but the problem body claims status 500.

steps.action: Run the known-good ten-request matrix first.
steps.reason: A baseline distinguishes a bad handler from a broken test.

steps.action: Inject status mismatch into a synthetic RFC 9457 body.
steps.reason: Problem status must match actual HTTP status.

steps.action: Drop the 401 auth challenge and retype the 201 amount field.
steps.reason: Headers and JSON primitive types are public contracts.

guidedPractice.prompt: What is wrong when HTTP status is 409 and problem.status equals 500?
hints: The field and the response line describe the same occurrence.
guidedPractice.explanation: The representation contradicts the actual response. The test must fail and the handler must produce a consistent status.

independentChallenge.prompt: Mutate GET account 200 to omit a required currency field and show the checker rejects it.
expectedEvidence: Three mutation rejections and a separately demonstrated missing required field failure.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: An omitted Account.currency differs from the Transfer.amount type mismatch worked example.

segments.firstAction: Compare the HTTP status and the problem body status from a negative response.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Sharing one generated response object between the stub and the test oracle without testing failure sensitivity.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: Both sides can drift together and still look green unless wrong responses are actively rejected.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Load the checked-in independent spec in the assertion boundary and add deliberate response mutations.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Three mutated responses fail the checker while normal wire cases pass.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Verify assert.throws wraps the validator and no malformed response bypasses schema or header checks.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Repeat the same test matrix against Spring MockMvc or a running isolated application.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Start with the RFC 9457 body-to-wire invariant, then verify Location and amount typing.

reviewQuestions.prompt: RFC 9110 mengenal 422 tetapi SYS-008 POST tidak mendeklarasikan 422. Bagaimana verdict-nya?
options: Lulus karena 422 adalah status HTTP valid
Laporkan gap kontrak; 422 butuh perubahan spec eksplisit
reviewQuestions.explanation: Status yang mungkin menurut RFC tidak otomatis menjadi respons yang dijanjikan oleh OpenAPI operasi ini.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Apa assertion penting saat POST /transfers mengembalikan HTTP 201?
options: Location mengarah ke ID yang ada di body dan schema Transfer valid
reviewQuestions.explanation: Location dan response schema adalah bagian observable contract; 201 tidak menyatakan transfer telah settled.

reviewQuestions.prompt: GET /accounts tanpa kredensial mengembalikan 401 tetapi tidak memiliki WWW-Authenticate. Apa hasilnya?
reviewQuestions.explanation: RFC 9110 mewajibkan challenge pada 401 dan SYS-008 juga mendeklarasikannya.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Problem body menyebut status 500 sementara response HTTP adalah 409. Apa tindakan checker?
options: Fail karena tidak konsisten menurut RFC 9457
reviewQuestions.explanation: Generator harus menyelaraskan nilai status yang disediakan dengan HTTP response code sebenarnya.

reviewQuestions.prompt: Apa yang terbukti ketika seluruh sepuluh live HTTP request pada stub Node lulus?
options: Spring MVC, JWT dan transaksi keuangan telah terbukti
Perilaku HTTP stub lokal sesuai subset kontrak, Spring/security/DB harus diuji terpisah
Semua consumer versi lama pasti kompatibel
reviewQuestions.explanation: Fixture berjalan di memory pada Node loopback dan belum menyentuh aplikasi Spring atau sistem pembayaran nyata.
